MD-12 triage. internal_regs_map exposes offsets 0x00-0x1ff while m_IOregs holds 64 entries and IOREG() indexes it unmasked. Prints sizeof(m_IOregs), the byte delta to m_shiftreg, and where each out-of-bounds offset actually lands, rather than inferring it from the class layout.
patches.added: 2026-10-14, authored outside this session; recorded by tests/test_mame_local_patches.py, which failed on it as designed

behaviour_changes.reason: The MD-12 memory-safety fix. m_IOregs grew from 64 to 0x200 entries and IOREG() now masks its offset to 0x1ff. Access below offset 0x40 is unaffected, and this game's GSP program writes at 0x90-0x160, so this changes the oracle's behaviour precisely where the unfixed build was running off the end of the array. It is a model fix, not an observation, and must never be filed under patches.

provenance_note: STUNRUN-IOB appeared in the MAME working tree while this session was running and was not authored here. It is recorded because an unrecorded hook in the oracle is exactly the failure tests/test_mame_local_patches.py exists to catch. Its observation-only status was read off its body, not assumed. The MD-12 fix is filed under behaviour_changes rather than patches for the same reason: the guard rejects any non-observation-only entry in patches, and calling this one observation-only would be false. Note that tms34010.h now appears in BOTH lists -- it carries observation hooks and a behavioural fix inside one diff, which is exactly the case the file-level check cannot detect on its own.
